title: Olaparib · adjuvant breast treatment
context_label: Germline BRCA1/2-associated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer
scope_note: These materials cover olaparib after treatment for high-risk early breast cancer. Other cancers use different eligibility, duration and follow-up; use the matching NCCP indication and your treating team’s plan.
schedule_summary: Take olaparib tablets morning and evening every day. There is no planned week off. Blood-review appointments are usually every four weeks during this one-year breast course.
purpose: Reduce the chance of invasive recurrence after standard chemotherapy and local treatment. It may be taken alongside prescribed endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive disease.
indication_text: NCCP 00588 h only: germline pathogenic BRCA1/2-associated HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer after neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy. Do not route other 00588 indications into this breast suite.
administration_text: Olaparib tablets 300 mg orally twice daily continuously, with source renal/toxicity/interaction adjustments. Tablets are not interchangeable with capsules. Breast duration:one year or earlier recurrence/unacceptable toxicity.
monitoring_summary: FBC, renal and liver profile every 4 weeks throughout the 12-month breast course; earlier/additional tests for symptoms or abnormal results. Review adherence, tablet supply, nausea, fatigue and all medicines. No routine olaparib-specific ECG, echo or DXA; follow separate previous/ongoing treatment risks. Breast surveillance continues after olaparib, without automatic asymptomatic CT or tumour-marker scheduling.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Olaparib (Lynparza)
agents.mechanism: Disrupts DNA repair in susceptible cancer cells
visual: DNA damage accumulates in cancer cells
agents.explanation: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help cells repair breaks in DNA. Some cancers with these changes rely more heavily on other repair routes. Olaparib inhibits PARP activity and traps PARP on DNA, making it harder for those cancer cells to survive DNA damage. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, which is why regular blood counts matter.
agents.watch: Keep the four-weekly blood reviews and report persistent nausea, marked fatigue, infections, bleeding or new respiratory symptoms. Severe blood abnormalities need review even if you feel well.
risks: Nausea, vomiting, reduced appetite and indigestion
Low neutrophils or platelets, with infection or bleeding risk
Uncommon but serious pneumonitis or drug-induced liver injury
Rare serious marrow disorders, including MDS/AML
Venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism; risk differs by treatment setting
Fetal harm; contraception and breastfeeding restrictions

anatomy: Ask for help early if nausea or vomiting makes it difficult to eat, drink or take tablets.
Anaemia can cause marked tiredness or breathlessness; low white cells and platelets can cause infection or bruising.
A new cough or worsening breathlessness needs prompt assessment; uncommon lung inflammation is important to recognise.
Report jaundice, dark urine or persistent upper abdominal discomfort; liver tests help investigate possible injury.

urgent_extra: Contact the oncology team urgently for fever or feeling acutely unwell, unusual bleeding, new or worsening breathlessness/cough, severe weakness, persistent vomiting or inability to drink. Chest pain, severe breathing difficulty or collapse require emergency help.

sections.title: After chemotherapy and local treatment
sections.text: Olaparib follows the chemotherapy and local-treatment plan. In OlympiA, surgery and any indicated radiotherapy were completed before olaparib, with at least a two-week gap after local treatment. NCCP advises starting ideally within twelve weeks of the last surgery, chemotherapy or radiation; your team sets the start.

sections.title: Endocrine therapy may overlap
sections.text: For hormone receptor-positive disease, the prescribed hormone treatment can continue alongside olaparib and often continues after the one-year olaparib course. Its injections, tablets and bone checks keep their own schedule.

sections.title: A daily routine at home
sections.text: Choose consistent morning and evening times and check the strength and number of tablets on each new prescription. Keep a sufficient supply before weekends or holidays. No infusion pump or port is needed for olaparib itself.

sections.title: If treatment is paused
sections.text: The oncology team decides when and at what dose to restart after blood recovery or symptom improvement. Do not calculate a catch-up dose or restart automatically because a calendar month has passed.

sections.title: After the planned year
sections.text: Agree the stop date and ongoing breast follow-up. Endocrine treatment and breast surveillance may continue. Report persistent unexplained fatigue, infections, bruising or breathlessness even after olaparib finishes.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be chosen
evidence.intro: In people with the high-risk inherited BRCA-associated breast cancer studied, one year of olaparib reduced invasive recurrence and improved survival. Longer follow-up shows that the benefit persists after treatment ends. Eligibility is specific, and benefit for an individual remains uncertain.
evidence.population: NCCP 00588 h only: germline pathogenic BRCA1/2-associated HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer after neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy. Do not route other 00588 indications into this breast suite.
evidence.interpretation: The treating team considers the cancer, previous treatment, health and your priorities. Trial averages do not predict an individual outcome.
evidence.limitations: Evidence is specific to the population and schedule studied. Discuss expected benefit, alternatives and uncertainty for your own treatment.

teachback: Which medicine is taken or given when, what checks are expected next, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: This patient suite is only for breast adjuvant indication 00588 h. Kidney/liver impairment, previous dose reductions and interacting medicines can change the dose. New blood abnormalities can occasionally signal a serious marrow problem and must be investigated. Olaparib can harm an unborn baby. Discuss effective contraception before treatment; EMA recommends two reliable complementary methods for women during treatment and for six months afterwards. Men and their partners need contraception during treatment and for three months afterwards. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for one month after the last dose.

support.title: Nausea support matched to oral treatment
support.text: NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high emetic risk. Agree an anti-sickness plan under local policy, and seek review if oral intake falls. The SmPC describes early/intermittent symptoms; do not automatically copy an intravenous chemotherapy antiemetic cycle.

support.title: Check the antiemetic interaction
support.text: Aprepitant is a moderate CYP3A inhibitor in NCCP 00588 and can increase olaparib exposure. The prescriber/pharmacist should choose and reconcile supportive medicines; never add an antiemetic from another regimen without checking.

support.title: Blood and infection support
support.text: Anaemia or other low counts can lead to interruption, dose adjustment, transfusion or additional investigation. There is no universal routine G-CSF course for every person on this regimen.

support.title: Medicines and supplements
support.text: Review all prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs and herbal products. Strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors or inducers can change exposure. Avoid grapefruit products and seek advice before starting anything new.

support.title: Stomach symptoms
support.text: NCCP allows consideration of a proton pump inhibitor under local policy. This is symptom- and patient-dependent, rather than a compulsory medication for everyone.

chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: Reduce the chance of invasive recurrence after standard chemotherapy and local treatment. It may be taken alongside prescribed endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive disease.

items.title: Who this covers
items.text: Adults with a confirmed pathogenic germline BRCA1/2 mutation, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer and previous neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy. The high-risk definition depends on hormone receptors, prior chemotherapy setting, surgical pathology and, for one pathway, CPS+EG score.

items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: Usually 300 mg twice daily; follow the individual prescription. Swallow tablets whole with water, with or without food. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. If a dose is missed, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double it. Check tablet strength after any dose change.

items.title: Duration and decisions
items.text: For breast indication 00588 h: up to one year, or earlier if the cancer recurs or side effects make treatment unsuitable. This is different from olaparib durations in ovarian, prostate and pancreatic cancer.

items.title: Individual safety and source differences
items.text: This patient suite is only for breast adjuvant indication 00588 h. Kidney/liver impairment, previous dose reductions and interacting medicines can change the dose. New blood abnormalities can occasionally signal a serious marrow problem and must be investigated.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Blood tests assess treatment safety. Scans assess disease or investigate symptoms. Echo and ECG answer different questions.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: Confirm the germline BRCA result and breast eligibility. Review blood count, kidney and liver tests, recovery from previous treatment, medicines and supplements, and pregnancy testing where relevant. Confirm the surgery/radiotherapy sequence and the planned start.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: NCCP specifies FBC, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first twelve months. Reviews also assess nausea, appetite, energy, bruising, infections and breathing symptoms. Extra tests or an interruption may be needed if results or symptoms change.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: Olaparib alone has no routine ECG or echo surveillance timetable in this NCCP regimen. Heart checks may still be needed because of previous anthracycline/HER2 treatment, existing disease or new symptoms.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: There is no olaparib-specific DXA schedule. If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is also prescribed, retain that treatment’s separate bone-density and bone-health plan.

chapters.title: Your wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Additional treatments depend on the confirmed setting and indication.

items.title: Early-breast follow-up
items.text: After early breast cancer treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation, or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. Routine mammography of the mastectomy side is not required. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended solely to look for recurrence in an asymptomatic person. Safety blood tests for ongoing olaparib are a separate requirement. New symptoms need assessment between appointments.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: No routine tumour-marker surveillance for asymptomatic early breast cancer.

items.title: Pregnancy, fertility and contraception
items.text: Olaparib can harm an unborn baby. Discuss effective contraception before treatment; EMA recommends two reliable complementary methods for women during treatment and for six months afterwards. Men and their partners need contraception during treatment and for three months afterwards. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for one month after the last dose.

chapters.title: Evidence depends on the population
chapters.intro: Different studies answer different questions; do not compare their results as if populations and follow-up were identical.

items.title: OlympiA: four-year survival analysis
items.text: The earlier survival update showed that the benefit extended beyond preventing invasive recurrence. These results apply to the selected high-risk inherited BRCA-associated early breast population, not every HER2-negative breast cancer.

items.title: OlympiA: sustained benefit at six years
items.text: Longer follow-up confirms that reductions in invasive recurrence and improvements in survival persist after the planned year of treatment. This is follow-up after one year of olaparib, not a longer prescribed course; rare late marrow effects still need attention.

chapters.title: Benefit, course and continuing checks
chapters.intro: In people with the high-risk inherited BRCA-associated breast cancer studied, one year of olaparib reduced invasive recurrence and improved survival. Longer follow-up shows that the benefit persists after treatment ends. Eligibility is specific, and benefit for an individual remains uncertain.

items.title: Before and during treatment
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile every 4 weeks throughout the 12-month breast course; earlier/additional tests for symptoms or abnormal results. Review adherence, tablet supply, nausea, fatigue and all medicines.

items.title: Heart checks and the full course
items.text: No routine olaparib-specific ECG, echo or DXA; follow separate previous/ongoing treatment risks. Breast surveillance continues after olaparib, without automatic asymptomatic CT or tumour-marker scheduling. High risk:TNBC residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy or node-positive/≥2 cm after adjuvant chemotherapy; HR-positive disease requires residual disease with CPS+EG≥3 after neoadjuvant therapy or≥4 positive nodes after adjuvant chemotherapy. Ideally start within 12 weeks of the last surgery, chemotherapy or radiation.

questions.q: When do I take or receive treatment?
questions.a: Take olaparib tablets morning and evening every day. There is no planned week off. Blood-review appointments are usually every four weeks during this one-year breast course. Swallow tablets whole with water, with or without food. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. If a dose is missed, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double it. Check tablet strength after any dose change.

questions.q: When are bloods, ECGs or echoes needed?
questions.a: Confirm the germline BRCA result and breast eligibility. Review blood count, kidney and liver tests, recovery from previous treatment, medicines and supplements, and pregnancy testing where relevant. Confirm the surgery/radiotherapy sequence and the planned start. NCCP specifies FBC, kidney and liver tests every four weeks for the first twelve months. Reviews also assess nausea, appetite, energy, bruising, infections and breathing symptoms. Extra tests or an interruption may be needed if results or symptoms change. Olaparib alone has no routine ECG or echo surveillance timetable in this NCCP regimen. Heart checks may still be needed because of previous anthracycline/HER2 treatment, existing disease or new symptoms.

After early breast cancer treatment, annual mammography is generally used for remaining breast tissue: both breasts after conservation, or the opposite breast after unilateral mastectomy. Routine mammography of the mastectomy side is not required. Routine CT, bone scans and tumour markers are not recommended solely to look for recurrence in an asymptomatic person. Safety blood tests for ongoing olaparib are a separate requirement. New symptoms need assessment between appointments.

For breast indication 00588 h: up to one year, or earlier if the cancer recurs or side effects make treatment unsuitable. This is different from olaparib durations in ovarian, prostate and pancreatic cancer.

questions.q: What should make me call today?
questions.a: Contact the oncology team urgently for fever or feeling acutely unwell, unusual bleeding, new or worsening breathlessness/cough, severe weakness, persistent vomiting or inability to drink. Chest pain, severe breathing difficulty or collapse require emergency help.
There is no olaparib-specific DXA schedule. If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is also prescribed, retain that treatment’s separate bone-density and bone-health plan.
